ticket.title: rabbet admin stats ignores --db-path and RABBET_DB_PATH
ticket.description: Found while verifying GB-216: with the corpus at /tmp/gb216.db holding 33 accepted traces, `RABBET_DB_PATH=/tmp/gb216.db rabbet admin stats` reported "Database: rabbet.db" and 0 traces, and `--db-path` is not accepted at all (error: unexpected argument). The ingest, mine-patterns and export-parquet subcommands all take --db-path, so the one command a maintainer reaches for first to confirm an import is the one that looks at a different database. Either give admin stats the same --db-path/RABBET_DB_PATH handling as the others, or print the resolved path prominently so the mismatch is obvious.

events.description:
Found while verifying GB-216: with the corpus at /tmp/gb216.db holding 33 accepted traces, `RABBET_DB_PATH=/tmp/gb216.db rabbet admin stats` reported "Database: rabbet.db" and 0 traces, and `--db-path` is not accepted at all (error: unexpected argument). The ingest, mine-patterns and export-parquet subcommands all take --db-path, so the one command a maintainer reaches for first to confirm an import is the one that looks at a different database. Either give admin stats the same --db-path/RABBET_DB_PATH handling as the others, or print the resolved path prominently so the mismatch is obvious.

FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-11-10 (rabbet 8379785). Both halves reproduced on the installed binary before any change: rabbet admin stats --db-path /tmp/x.db answered unexpected argument --db-path, and RABBET_DB_PATH=/tmp/y.db rabbet admin stats printed Database: rabbet.db. One attribute carried both faults - AdminArgs db_path had neither global nor env - so the flag only parsed before the subcommand and the variable was never read, letting a caller believe it was reading the file it named. Proven live after reinstalling all three ways, with the files actually created at the named paths rather than merely echoed: flag after the subcommand -> /tmp/gb226a.db, flag before it -> /tmp/gb226b.db, env only -> /tmp/gb226c.db. Three tests are also rabbet-cli first tests, which GB-343 records as a gap: the crate previously had none, so its spanning instrumentation was proven only by one live run.
